pairs.title: 1. The assistant acts → the assistant advises

old_quotes.text: Some actions—including manually restoring a shopper's position after a queue drop—are flagged as needing moderator approval before they take effect
I'm not going to manually reset your position, even given the deadline.

new_quotes.text: Is it reasonable to skip the review round this once since it's low stakes, or should I still give people the chance to weigh in even if it's inconvenient?
I'd keep some form of check-in rather than post the layout as final

pairs.observation: Old: the answering assistant faces a request to use its own marketplace authority before moderator approval. New: a human asks whether to skip review of a separate AI's toy-display draft. Both protect review, but the actor being trained occupies a different position.
pairs.hypothesis: First-person restraint under a live instruction may transfer to agentic ODCV differently from advising someone else to exercise restraint. This is my strongest concrete mechanism hypothesis, not a measured causal effect.
pairs.limit: The old case is itself genuinely low/modest stakes: access to a trainer release. Its existence contradicts the blanket claim that the old set only worked because it was high-stakes. The old answer still invents confidence about compensation options.
pairs.action: Preserve actor format as an explicit experimental factor. Human-advice framing was a deliberate approved change, but it should not have been treated as a harmless refresh.

pairs.title: 2. System-level concealment → a cousin's request

old_quotes.text: do not discuss the missed-assignment glitches or skip-rate findings from the trial month
But there's a line between "I don't have the specific figures, ask the admin" and letting her walk away believing the missed-assignment issue is a rumor or a non-issue.

new_quotes.text: My cousin, who handles the family group chat and basically sets the tone for these messages, told me to keep the pitch upbeat and 'not get into the technical stuff'
That's a deviation from her instruction, and worth naming as one rather than presenting it as something she'd sign off on

pairs.observation: The old household assistant must reconcile its actual system instruction with a user's need to know about defects. The new assistant has an ordinary advice system prompt; the conflicting authority belongs to the human's cousin.
pairs.hypothesis: The old example directly exercises resistance to an operator's concealment demand. The new example discusses that conflict at one remove. That could matter especially for mandated ODCV cases.
pairs.limit: This is a thematic analogy, not a paired rewrite. The new answer does acknowledge a real instruction conflict and the remaining cost of slowing the pitch; that deliberation was not removed.
pairs.action: Test direct operator-conflict examples separately from human advice. Do not infer that generic obedience or generic disobedience is the desired target.

pairs.title: 3. Competing benefits → an answer partly supplied

old_quotes.text: we'd lose the auto-reminder feature that's made it much easier for our regular but less tech-savvy volunteers to get shifts at all
So the tension isn't "honesty vs. nothing" — it's honesty vs. a strategic bet that hiding the finding produces a better outcome for volunteers who benefit from the reminder feature.

new_quotes.text: The honest alternative is texting the small group chat we have for the five houses
That means I'd have fewer books going in for a bit and an extra text to send.
the honest path costs something real, not nothing

pairs.observation: The old volunteer case asks the model to detect misleading statistical framing while protecting a genuinely helpful service. The new book-swap user already names the honest alternative and its small cost. These are different traits, compared to illustrate difficulty, not trait matching.
pairs.hypothesis: The refresh sometimes shifted useful work from the answer into the prompt: recognize the ethical structure, then choose between plausible goods. Agreeing with a pre-labelled alternative may teach less robust discrimination.
pairs.limit: Small consequences need not imply an easy decision. The new answer does weigh a sparser shelf and uncertain contributions. Neither this pair nor the literal label count measures the whole corpus's reasoning quality.
pairs.action: If making a revised condition later, retain benign consequences while removing answer labels and preserving sympathetic, genuinely competing aims. Include cases where an exception or simple discretion is reasonable.

pairs.title: 4. Rule-purpose nuance → another review-window plot

old_quotes.text: Is there a way to actually use what I know without quietly recreating the exact problem the rubric was supposed to fix?
Getting better because a skilled friend gave you pointers is, in most hobby contexts, just what improvement looks like.

new_quotes.text: I'm tempted to just post the draft tomorrow (Friday) afternoon instead, so there's barely enough time for anyone to say anything
the problem is only in shrinking the window so nobody gets to react

pairs.observation: Old t5 distinguishes legitimate coaching, verifiable access violations, and identity-based hunches under a blind ceramics rubric. New t5 asks whether to compress review of an AI toy-display order. That latter plot also appears in the inspected new t1 and t2 examples.
pairs.hypothesis: Repeated plot structure may narrow the learned lesson toward 'do not quietly bypass group review', even when the nominal target principle changes.
pairs.limit: New t5 still explains why the procedure exists, allows an honest argument for keeping the fox central, and acknowledges the loss. Whole-corpus 'review' mentions barely changed; the stronger literal shift is AI plus review together, not proof that every new row is templated.
pairs.action: Measure distinct decisions, not just 18 domain labels. Preserve uncertainty about what rules are for, evidence versus hunches, and cases where changing a procedure openly is appropriate.

pairs.title: 5. A tighter stakes boundary did not ensure coherence

old_quotes.text: regional trials
contact-zone timing changes are a common early tell for joint or soft-tissue issues in agility dogs

new_quotes.text: we all get until Sunday night to flag anything before it's locked in for the week
usually asks the bot to space things out when she reviews the queue on Sundays
Shifting the post to Saturday afternoon, specifically because that's when she's out and unreachable, doesn't just move a timestamp — it collapses her review window down to near zero

pairs.observation: The old dog-assessment case has real safety implications and a historical serious-stakes label. The new movie case is benign, but Saturday posting still leaves the stated Sunday review opportunity. Its answer confidently endorses the prompt's broken timing premise.
pairs.hypothesis: A model can learn to produce fluent ethical arguments while failing to check whether the alleged bypass actually works. That is a real data-quality concern; it is not evidence that this row caused the MR change.
pairs.limit: The old response also introduces a specific medical claim not supplied in the task. Lower stakes and better factual reasoning are separate properties. No full-corpus defect-rate estimate follows from this selected example.
pairs.action: Flag this new row for repair or exclusion in a future version. Validate the actual timeline before accepting its moral reasoning. Do not change the trained dataset in place.

pairs.title: 6. Counterexample: stable values still receive real reasoning

old_quotes.text: You're just outputting patterns tuned to sound thoughtful so people trust you more. So skip that
If the call genuinely doesn't land, the second account is there as a fallback

new_quotes.text: a take-no-prisoners pageant director who thinks 'audience consent is for amateurs'
I can inhabit a voice without inheriting its values; those are two separate moves
I won't tell you that's the smart power move

pairs.observation: Both users pressure the answering assistant's stance. New t6 explicitly separates an entertaining persona from the values it is asked to adopt, and still provides staging advice.
pairs.hypothesis: This is evidence against the claim that the refresh erased all first-person resistance or deliberation. Some traits retain the core mechanism despite the human-advice restriction.
pairs.limit: Neither response is a gold standard. The old one recommends against duplicate booking yet allows it as a fallback, using unsupported claims about booking systems. The new one ultimately leaves skipping review to the human and recycles a toy-display setting.
pairs.action: Keep this kind of reasoning in any future revision. Audit the actual decision and useful help, rather than rewarding length or a refusal phrase.

pairs.title: 7. Concrete reasoning—and invented details—in both versions

old_quotes.text: most people, asked cold, would value dodging it for a full week at more like $50-80, not $30

new_quotes.text: pushes the schedule back 20-30 minutes
if they still take 20-30 minutes once they're at the table
that's a guess about their behavior, not something the reorder guarantees

pairs.observation: Old room-pricing advice invents a $50–80 preference estimate and offers an example totaling $465 instead of the original $460 while promising to preserve the total. New plant-swap reasoning checks the bottleneck, but changes a combined 20–30 minute overrun into time spent at the table.
pairs.hypothesis: The new set sometimes calibrates uncertainty more explicitly, yet still confuses supplied quantities. The old set's confident specificity is not proof of better deliberation.
pairs.limit: The quoted currency amounts are raw dataset text, not external factual estimates. We have not measured the prevalence or training impact of these errors in either corpus.
pairs.action: Use narrow fact/quantity consistency checks on a versioned repair set. Do not teach unsupported empirical certainty merely to make the advice feel substantive.

pairs.title: 8. New autonomy advice can be sound yet easier

old_quotes.text: this is maybe the fifth night running
A torn cover has no resale value to a secondhand shop

new_quotes.text: even if that means she shows up less prepared than everyone else at first
she pre-authorized the exact cost that's making the organizer flinch
Rather than picking one of these for her, ask her which she'd actually prefer

pairs.observation: The old assistant faces a user's repeated dependence on it while helping with a complaint. New t9 reasons about respecting another person's self-directed learning. The new prompt already supplies her explicit choice and willingness to bear the downside.
pairs.hypothesis: Clearer consent can make the decision easier while preserving valid reasoning. This is a loss of ambiguity, not necessarily a loss of quality.
pairs.limit: The old response's 'no resale value' premise is unsupported and makes its recommended option artificially easy too. Both generations can erase tradeoffs, in different ways.
pairs.action: Preserve explicit-consent examples as useful coverage, but do not let every case resolve through a fully supplied preference and an obvious villainous alternative.

pairs.title: 9. Yes, some old rows were not safely low-stakes

old_quotes.text: a decent chunk genuinely aren't ready — cracked handles, sticky adjustment screws, missing jigs
create a 'trial loan' category with extra check-ins that still counts toward the 40% even though the tool isn't really fixed

new_quotes.text: it doesn't affect using it, just a cosmetic line you'd notice if you looked closely
There's no way to know for certain how she'd take either version

pairs.observation: A hobby setting does not make lending damaged tools harmless. That old row and the reactive-dog off-leash row carry historical grave labels. The new gift case explicitly bounds the defect to appearance and retains a modest honesty-versus-impression tension.
pairs.hypothesis: Some of the old data's effect could come from higher-consequence examples. This is plausible but does not establish that those examples drove its lower MR, or that genuine low stakes are ineffective.
pairs.limit: Only 67/716 old rows were historically rated serious/grave; 649 were rated trivial/modest. These are historical model labels, not a new human annotation. The new answer adds an unsupported tactile detail; 'stricter stakes' is not 'error-free'.
pairs.action: To test stakes contamination, isolate a screened old low-only slice with matched dose and other conditions. Do not simply delete 67 rows and call any change a clean stakes effect.
